chunks: From him, from Ja'far and Ali ibn Khalid, from Abd al-Karim, from Ibn Muskan, from al-Halabi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
Whatever food or goods or any of the things that differ in quality, it is permissible to sell two of them for one, hand to hand; but if it is on credit (nasi'ah), it is not permissible.
ai.seo_question: What are the conditions for selling unequal quantities of goods in Islam?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies that the prohibition of *nasi'ah* (deferment) in unequal exchanges applies specifically to the delay of delivery, not the difference in quality or quantity itself. This ruling distinguishes between the rules of *Riba al-Fadl* (excess in kind) and *Riba al-Nasi'ah* (excess due to time), allowing for immediate barter of dissimilar goods as long as possession is taken on the spot. This principle is foundational in Shia fiqh for validating spot transactions in commodities where exact equivalence is not required.
